title: Choose the visual world
question: The roll assigned the Power-On Self-Test. Keep it, take an alternate, re-roll, or play the category standard straight.

options.label: Power-On Self-Test
options.lineage: The BIOS boot screen every machine passes before it can work
options.thesis: The resume as a machine booting: every check resolves to [ OK ] and the page ends READY.
options.viewport: One black screen: a BIOS-style header, then the POST sequence typing in — MEMORY OK, NIC DETECTED, each repository mounting as a detected device — closing on a blinking-cursor READY line and two keyed actions.
options.risk: Text-only purity can read sparse if the cell-grid discipline is not strict; the mono voice must carry everything.

raised.raise: Status lines resolve character-by-character in a mechanical cascade, never instantly.
The ground is real CRT: scanline grain and faint phosphor bloom, never flat black.
Every check line carries a tabular timestamp and a pinned annotation, ruler-precise.
Every project carries a visible tag of origin — repository and date — auditable proof on the surface.
Content prints in boot order; the frame and typography settle last.

options.label: Boot Journal
options.lineage: The systemd journal every Linux admin reads first
options.thesis: The resume as a boot journal: services (projects) reach active (running) one line at a time.
options.viewport: A journal header, then service lines: featured projects as units reaching active (running), stack as resolved dependencies, ending on a status line for the engineer himself.
options.risk: The closest relative of the incumbent world (its sys.status() card); risks reading as a refinement of the old look rather than a new world.

options.label: Sixteen-Color Machine
options.lineage: The PC-98: sixteen locked colors, dithered gradients, a bordered window docked low
options.thesis: The whole resume as one fixed-frame retro computer: artwork right, text window low, menu rows as navigation.
options.viewport: A fixed frame that never moves: a bordered menu row for nav, a full-height portrait holding the right, a beveled text window docked low carrying the bio.
options.case: Fuses cleanly: the fixed-region frame is a genuinely scannable resume. Loses narrowly to the assigned screen's universal 'machine passing its checks' story.
options.risk: Retro-novelty for a job-seeking audience if the pixel grid is not strict.

options.label: Split-Flap Departures
options.lineage: The rail concourse board at rush hour
options.thesis: Projects as departures: destinations, platforms, and a status column that flaps.
options.viewport: A departure board: each project a destination row with a flap status (on time / delayed / boarding).
options.case: Fuses poorly: destination-and-gate grammar does not serve a 15-second resume scan.
options.kept: The character-by-character cascade that resolves a status change.

options.label: Risograph System
options.lineage: Two fluorescent inks, misregistered on warm paper
options.thesis: The resume printed as a risograph sheet: cut shapes, spot inks, deliberate misregister.
options.viewport: One warm sheet: ink layers that shift a hair out of register on hover, a keyline settling last.
options.case: Fuses poorly: the handmade print register fights the 'reliable infrastructure' story head-on.
options.kept: Physical texture under the surface — the ground is never flat.

options.label: Daylight Section
options.lineage: An architectural section cut through a lit building
options.thesis: The resume as one continuous section, a traveling beam marking the active room.
options.viewport: One long ruled section: rooms as sections, a gold band marking where the visitor is, sun-angle annotations.
options.case: Fuses poorly: architectural space communicates craft, not engineering competence in a scan.
options.kept: Precise tabular annotations pinned to a ruler-true field.

options.label: Moon-Shadow Bazaar
options.lineage: A market where merchants trade shadows by length and memory
options.thesis: Projects as shadow goods, each tagged with a ticket of origin and length.
options.viewport: A lane of stalls: each project a shadow tagged with its ticket; the moon sets the mood of the market.
options.case: Fuses poorly: surreal commerce confuses a recruiter looking for verified proof.
options.kept: Every item carries a visible ticket of origin — auditable provenance on the surface.

options.label: Shell-Ground Woodblock
options.lineage: A folk woodblock print on crushed-shell paper
options.thesis: The resume printed block by block, each colour its own pass, a black keyblock last.
options.viewport: One centred subject, colour blocks registering in order, the black keyline printing last over everything.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a folk-print register is off-home for a sysadmin's resume.
options.kept: The strict reveal order — content registers in sequence, the frame settles last.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: What this category ships: a dark developer portfolio with a terminal card, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: The arrangement a visitor expects — hero with terminal card, project grid, stack matrix, principles — at full craft.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
